end.parentNote: Ishita practised showing sequence growth with rows, columns, and dots. They correctly used the shared corner to explain why adding a row and column counts one dot twice, and used an L-shaped picture to justify 16 + 9 = 25. An initial count of the new row and column was mixed up, then corrected later by identifying the shared corner. At home, ask them to draw a 4×4 square and add one row and column, explaining the overlap.
